title: The Riverside Safe
overview: A neighborhood theater's payroll cash disappears from a locked office safe overnight. The alarm records a brief power interruption, but there is no forced entry.
objective: Determine whether the safe was opened during a genuine outage or by someone using authorized access to disguise a theft.

hypotheses.statement: Night manager Tessa Quinn used the maintenance key during a planned power interruption to take the payroll cash.
An unknown burglar entered through the loading bay during an accidental power outage.

evidence.title: Theft report
evidence.content: Payroll cash was missing from the Riverside Theater office safe at opening. The safe and office door showed no damage.

evidence.title: Closing staff roster
evidence.content: Night manager Tessa Quinn and technician Andre Bell closed the theater. Both had access to the building; only the manager held the safe override key.

evidence.title: Power and alarm logs
evidence.content: The office circuit was manually isolated for four minutes at 11:37 PM. The building's other circuits stayed online and the alarm was disarmed with a manager code.

evidence.title: Loading bay inspection
evidence.content: The loading bay was secured from inside. Dust and seal marks around the door were undisturbed; no outside entry was detected.

evidence.title: Maintenance key register
evidence.content: The safe override key was checked out by Tessa Quinn and returned the following morning. The return time was recorded before the cash shortage was reported.

suspects.name: Tessa Quinn
suspects.role: Night manager with safe override access

witness_statements.statement: The office was locked and the safe had no signs of forced entry when the shortage was found.

timeline.event: The office circuit was manually isolated and alarm disarmed.
The manager safe key was checked out and returned.
